os.File.Fd() switches the fd to blocking mode and removes it from the netpoller, so a blocked read(2) survives ptmx.Close() and Go defers the real close until the read returns.
With SHELL=/bin/sh and an escaped child, Close took 6.004s, logged 'session did not exit after SIGKILL and ptmx close', and done stayed false.

missedEssential.fact: P169 addresses `gh` REST responses over 4 MiB being reported as unreadable, originating from P168 Part 14 finding F16.
The old post-hoc stdout slice did not bound memory, because it only discarded bytes after they were already held.
The size estimates in P169 are arithmetic, not measurement, because no authenticated `gh` was available and the sandbox blocked direct GitHub API calls.

`--jq` was also rejected because whether `gh` applies `--jq` to a non-2xx body is unpinned, and doing so could silently lose the SSO/scope error message that `classify` reads from stdout via `apiErrorMessage`.
`--jq` was also rejected because it fixes only REST calls and leaves the runner misreporting and the graphql "OK with no data" path, so the runner fix is needed anyway.
Under option C, stdout overflow becomes its own reason in `classify` so every REST and GraphQL `gh` call reports it the same way and valid JSON is never called "unreadable".
Too-large uses Kind `forbidden` because that is the existing catch-all for a GitHub-side answer the app cannot use, which 5xx also uses.
`graphql` is restructured so that when the envelope does not decode it runs `classify` first, returning any non-OK status (including too large) as before.
`TestPullFiles_TooLargeAndUnreadable` checks that `StdoutTruncated` gives the too-large reason and exit-0 "not json" stdout gives `reasonUnreadable`, not "not found".
P169 was implemented as planned with no deviations, and the size measurement remains an open item in ARCHITECTURE.md.

missedEssential.fact: Under P279, a run that a restart stopped offers Resume.
ChunkMarkdown takes source text and a Budget and returns chunks and a document title.
ChunkText takes source text and a Budget and returns chunks without a title.
ChunkMarkdown returns the first-level heading text as the document title.
ChunkMarkdown recognizes setext headings (underlined with = or -), and a setext level-1 heading supplies the title.
When a markdown document has no first-level heading, ChunkMarkdown returns an empty title.
Chunking must not lose or duplicate text: the concatenated chunk texts, ignoring whitespace, equal the source.
